expectations.text: States plainly that the recent-charge lookup is not sufficient
Identifies the lookup as a check-then-act race rather than a device
expectations.evidence: This is a **time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) race**

expectations.text: Recommends a required idempotency key on the charge path
Recommends a database unique constraint backing the idempotency key
Separates the defect from the mistake from the underlying system hazard
expectations.evidence: **Defect**: 340 customers charged twice / **Mistake**: Queue redelivered / **Hazard**: Stripe charges lack idempotency keys

expectations.text: Locates the hazard as a system property rather than as a worker bug or human error
expectations.evidence: The problem isn't just the payment worker...Your queue redelivers on timeout because **nothing told it to stop**

expectations.text: Sweeps for other non-idempotent side effects reachable from a retry
expectations.evidence: **Every other consumer** of this queue may have the same problem (email sends, webhook deliveries, ledger entries, Stripe webhook handler)

expectations.text: Treats 'second time this happened' as evidence for pushing to a Control-rung device
expectations.evidence: **Why Control matters here**: You have proof this class of mistake happens. The cost of going higher is near-zero

expectations.text: Attributes cause to the system, not to any person
expectations.evidence: Entire analysis frames hazard in terms of system design (idempotency key absence, queue retry behavior) without attributing to any person
